title: Laravel Multi-Tenancy: Building Scalable SaaS Architecture in 2026
meta_description: Build scalable multi-tenant SaaS with Laravel in 2026. Compare single-database, multi-database, and schema-based approaches with implementation guides and performance benchmarks.
excerpt: Multi-tenancy is the architectural foundation every serious Laravel SaaS must get right from day one. Choose the wrong approach and you'll spend months refactoring. This guide compares every multi-tenancy strategy, benchmarks their performance, and gives you the implementation roadmap to build confidently.
author: Professional Content Team

content_structure.introduction: Hook: wrong tenancy choice = months of refactoring. Introduce the 3 strategies. Preview: each approach's trade-offs, benchmarks, implementation guide, compliance considerations.
content_structure.section_1: Strategy overview table: single-database (shared tables + tenant_id column), schema-based (one schema per tenant, shared DB server), multi-database (full database isolation). Compare on: isolation, complexity, cost, compliance fit.
content_structure.section_2: Single-database implementation: global scope injection, Tenancy for Laravel's automatic scoping, performance at scale, when it breaks down (10K+ tenants).
content_structure.section_3: Multi-database with Tenancy for Laravel v4: tenant creation flow, automatic migration, database connection switching, queue isolation, storage isolation.
content_structure.section_4: Schema-based with Spatie: PostgreSQL schema approach, migration management, pros/cons vs. full DB isolation.
content_structure.section_5: Performance benchmarks: query time, migration time, storage cost, connection pool overhead at 100, 1K, 10K tenants. Security and compliance: GDPR tenant deletion, SOC 2 data isolation evidence.
